assay_or_method: heterologous expression in S. cerevisiae S150-2B (ADH1 promoter); substrates: gelatin, fibronectin, laminin, FaDu epithelial cells, endothelial cells
result: Adherence above background to laminin only; not to the other four substrates
quote: Als9p-expressing S. cerevisiae adhered above background levels only to laminin
what_it_supports: Direct experimental (gain-of-function, heterologous) adhesion evidence for ALS9: supports evidence_level E1 for ALS9. Binding is narrow (one of five substrates)
limits: Heterologous host, not C. albicans. Fig. 1 percentages were not extracted from the text. No ALS9 deletion in this paper

result: Surface expression detected: 11.4% of cells above background (4-fold) with antiserum A; 33.9% (13-fold) with antiserum B
what_it_supports: Shows the adherence result is not a failure of surface display. It was the weakest antiserum A signal of the six, so the paper's own caution on expression level applies
limits: Table II values copied from the paper's table

assay_or_method: endothelial cell invasion by S. cerevisiae expressing Als proteins
result: Text names Als3p, Als1p and Als5p as adhering to endothelial cells and Als3p (more) and Als1p, Als5p (less) as invasive. Als9p is not named as invasive
quote: organisms expressing Als3p and, to a lesser extent, Als1p and Als5p demonstrated significant endothelial cell invasion
what_it_supports: Als9p did not mediate endothelial adherence (see adhesion row). Invasion by Als9p is not reported in the text
limits: Fig. 3 itself was not read; the statement rests on the text only

assay_or_method: homology modelling of N-terminal domain; knowledge-based search (Table III)
result: N-terminal domain models as anti-parallel beta-sheet (immunoglobulin-superfamily-like). Homologs: S. aureus collagen-binding protein (PDB 1d2p; statistically significant), Y. pseudotuberculosis invasin/integrin-binding protein (1cwv), M. mazei surface layer protein (1L0QA). Als2p and Als9p share an identical primary, secondary and tertiary homolog
quote: only Als2p and Als9p shared an identical primary, secondary, and tertiary homolog
what_it_supports: Mechanism context: the paper locates substrate specificity in the folded N-terminal domain (single-interface binding), not in the repeats. Relevant to the label 2a (repeat/avidity) versus a folded binding domain
limits: Computational model only. Structure of Als9p was not solved here

result: The N termini of Als2p, Als4p and Als9p form a third structural group (group C), unlike group A (Als1/3/5) and group B (Als6/7)
quote: the N termini of Als2p, Als4p, and Als9p appear to constitute a third group of Als proteins (the Als group C)
what_it_supports: Als9p belongs to a structurally distinct subgroup, so Als1p repeat results cannot be assumed for Als9p

result: The paper does not state that ALS9 has tandem repeats or give its repeat copy number. It says ALS genes have tandem repeats in general, and that this made ALS2 and ALS4 hard to clone
quote: the difficulty of sequencing and assembling across the tandem repeats of ALS genes
what_it_supports: No protein-level statement of repeats for ALS9. The class 2a label for ALS9 stays a family inference (evidence_basis family_inference)
limits: The ALS9 row's current mechanism source, PMID 15116430, is the ALS1 paper (20 tandem repeats of 36 aa in Als1p), not an ALS9 paper
